question: Under O.C.G.A. § 43-40-18(b), what must a broker demonstrate to avoid being held responsible for an affiliated licensee's violation of Chapter 43-40?
choice_a: Only that the broker was unaware the violation occurred, regardless of any supervisory procedures
choice_b: Only that the affiliated licensee has already been individually disciplined by GREC for the same conduct
choice_c: That reasonable supervisory procedures were in place, that the broker did not participate in the violation, and that the broker did not ratify the violation
choice_d: That the affiliated licensee was terminated within 24 hours of the violation being discovered
explanation: O.C.G.A. § 43-40-18(b) creates a genuine statutory safe harbor, not strict liability: the broker must show (1) reasonable supervisory procedures were in place, (2) the broker did not participate in the violation, and (3) the broker did not ratify it, to avoid responsibility for the affiliate's violation.

question: A broker had documented, reasonable supervisory procedures in place, but personally participated in an affiliated licensee's violation of Chapter 43-40. Can the broker rely on the § 43-40-18(b) safe harbor to avoid responsibility?
choice_a: Yes -- having reasonable supervisory procedures in place is sufficient on its own, regardless of the broker's personal involvement
choice_b: Yes, as long as the broker did not personally profit from the violation
choice_c: No, but only because the broker also failed to notify GREC within 30 days
choice_d: No -- the safe harbor requires all three elements together, including that the broker did not participate in the violation; personal participation defeats the defense regardless of documented procedures
explanation: The § 43-40-18(b) safe harbor requires the broker to satisfy all three elements: reasonable supervisory procedures, no participation in the violation, and no ratification. A broker who personally participated cannot rely on the defense even with documented procedures in place.

question: A broker did not participate in an affiliated licensee's violation but, after learning of it, approved and endorsed the licensee's conduct after the fact. Does this defeat the § 43-40-18(b) safe harbor?
choice_a: Yes -- ratifying the violation after the fact defeats the safe harbor even without direct participation
choice_b: No -- ratification after the fact is irrelevant as long as the broker did not participate in the original act
choice_c: No -- ratification only matters if it occurs within 30 days of the original violation
choice_d: Yes, but only if the ratification was made in writing
explanation: The statutory safe harbor under § 43-40-18(b) requires that the broker neither participated in nor ratified the violation. Approving or endorsing the licensee's conduct after learning of it constitutes ratification, which independently defeats the safe harbor even absent direct participation.

question: Under O.C.G.A. § 43-40-18(c), a broker's required supervisory procedures must include a program covering which advertising-related duty?
choice_a: Approving only advertising that exceeds a certain dollar budget
choice_b: Reviewing all advertising produced by the firm and its affiliated licensees
choice_c: Reviewing advertising solely at the end of each calendar year
choice_d: Delegating all advertising review permanently to a third-party marketing vendor with no broker oversight
explanation: O.C.G.A. § 43-40-18(c) requires the broker/qualifying broker to establish and implement procedures for reviewing all advertising produced by the firm, as one of the enumerated supervisory duties.

question: Among the supervisory procedures required under O.C.G.A. § 43-40-18(c), what must a broker provide regarding license law?
choice_a: A one-time orientation session covering only office policies, with no license-law content required
choice_b: Reimbursement of licensees' personal continuing education costs
choice_c: Study or review programs on license law for affiliated licensees
choice_d: A written waiver excusing licensees from independently knowing license law, since the broker is solely responsible
explanation: O.C.G.A. § 43-40-18(c) requires the broker to establish and implement study or review programs on license law for affiliated licensees, as part of the required supervisory procedures.

question: Under O.C.G.A. § 43-40-18(c), within how many days of the offer or contract date must a broker review listing contracts, leases, sales contracts, management agreements, and offers?
explanation: O.C.G.A. § 43-40-18(c) requires the broker's supervisory procedures to include review of all listing contracts, leases, sales contracts, management agreements, and offers within 30 days of the offer or contract date.

question: A sales contract is dated March 1. Under O.C.G.A. § 43-40-18(c), by what date must the qualifying broker have reviewed that contract as part of the firm's required supervisory procedures?
choice_a: March 31 (within 30 days of the contract date)
choice_b: March 11 (within 10 days of the contract date)
choice_c: April 30 (within 60 days of the contract date)
choice_d: There is no specific deadline as long as the review occurs before closing
explanation: Under O.C.G.A. § 43-40-18(c), the broker must review contracts, listings, leases, management agreements, and offers within 30 days of the offer or contract date -- for a March 1 contract, that review must occur by March 31.

question: Which supervisory procedure does O.C.G.A. § 43-40-18(c) require regarding a firm's trust accounting practices?
choice_a: A single annual audit performed exclusively by an outside CPA, with no internal review permitted
choice_b: Systematic review of trust accounting practices
choice_c: No specific trust accounting review procedure is required beyond the general recordkeeping duty
choice_d: Review of trust accounting only when a client files a written complaint
explanation: O.C.G.A. § 43-40-18(c) requires the broker to establish and implement procedures for systematic review of the firm's trust accounting practices, as one of the enumerated supervisory duties.

question: Under O.C.G.A. § 43-40-18(c), a broker's supervisory procedures must ensure that compensation for licensed acts is paid only to a licensee under what condition?
choice_a: To any individual who assisted with the transaction, licensed or not, as long as the broker approves
choice_b: Only to licensees who have completed at least 5 years of active licensure
choice_c: Only to a licensee whose license was assigned to the firm at the time the compensation was earned
choice_d: To the firm's operating account only, with no direct payment to individual licensees permitted
explanation: O.C.G.A. § 43-40-18(c) requires supervisory procedures ensuring that only licensed personnel perform licensed acts, and that compensation is paid only to a licensee whose license was assigned to the firm at the time the compensation was earned.

question: Among the enumerated supervisory duties in O.C.G.A. § 43-40-18(c), what must a broker's procedures ensure regarding trust fund disbursements?
choice_a: That trust disbursements occur only once per calendar quarter, regardless of transaction timing
choice_b: That trust disbursements are made solely at the discretion of the affiliated licensee, without broker involvement
choice_c: That trust disbursements are always paid directly to the broker before being forwarded to the rightful party
choice_d: That proper trust disbursements are made
explanation: O.C.G.A. § 43-40-18(c) requires the broker's supervisory procedures to ensure that proper trust disbursements are made, as one of the enumerated required procedures.

question: What recordkeeping duty does O.C.G.A. § 43-40-18(c) impose on a broker as part of the required supervisory procedures?
choice_b: Destroying transaction records within 90 days of closing to reduce liability exposure
choice_c: Delegating all recordkeeping to individual licensees with no firm-level retention
choice_d: Maintaining records solely in the personal custody of each affiliated licensee, never centrally
explanation: O.C.G.A. § 43-40-18(c) enumerates safekeeping of records among the supervisory procedures a broker must establish and implement.

question: Under O.C.G.A. § 43-40-18(c), what must a broker ensure regarding the availability of personnel who hold management authority within the firm?
choice_a: That management-authority personnel are physically on-site at all firm locations at all times
choice_b: That management-authority personnel are reasonably available to assist licensees and the public
choice_c: That only the qualifying broker personally, and no delegate, may ever interact with the public
choice_d: That management-authority personnel are available only during the firm's first year of operation
explanation: O.C.G.A. § 43-40-18(c) requires the broker's procedures to ensure that personnel with management authority are reasonably available to assist licensees and the public -- one of the enumerated supervisory duties.

question: A qualifying broker delegates day-to-day supervisory duties to an office manager. Under O.C.G.A. § 43-40-18(d), does this delegation relieve the broker of ultimate responsibility for those duties?
choice_a: Yes -- once duties are formally delegated in writing, the broker bears no further responsibility
choice_b: Yes, but only if the office manager is also a licensed broker
choice_c: No -- a broker may delegate these duties but remains responsible for the delegate's acts
choice_d: No, but only until the office manager completes their own CE renewal cycle
explanation: O.C.G.A. § 43-40-18(d) confirms that a broker may delegate supervisory duties, but the broker remains responsible for the delegate's acts -- delegation does not eliminate ultimate broker responsibility.

question: Under Ga. Comp. R. & Regs. 520-1-.07(2), who is held responsible for an affiliated licensee's violation of license law, and what must that person also do regarding license-law instruction?
choice_a: Only the individual licensee who committed the violation bears responsibility; the broker has no instructional duty
choice_b: GREC itself is responsible for instructing all licensees directly, relieving brokers of any instructional role
choice_c: Responsibility falls on the firm's designated compliance officer only if one has been formally appointed
choice_d: The broker/qualifying broker is held responsible for the affiliate's violations, and must instruct affiliated licensees on license law and rules
explanation: Ga. Comp. R. & Regs. 520-1-.07(2) holds the broker/qualifying broker responsible for an affiliated licensee's violations and requires the broker to instruct affiliated licensees on license law and rules.

question: Under Ga. Comp. R. & Regs. 520-1-.07(2), what must a broker do upon learning of a violation of license law by an affiliated licensee?
choice_b: Handle the matter entirely internally, with no obligation to inform GREC
choice_c: Wait until the firm's next renewal period to report any known violations
choice_d: Report the violation only if the affiliated licensee consents to disclosure
explanation: Ga. Comp. R. & Regs. 520-1-.07(2) requires the broker/qualifying broker to notify GREC of any violation by an affiliated licensee -- this duty exists independent of any internal handling of the matter.

question: A firm's qualifying broker unexpectedly resigns. Under Ga. Comp. R. & Regs. 520-1-.07(3), how much time does the firm have to secure a new qualifying broker before it must cease brokerage activity?
explanation: Ga. Comp. R. & Regs. 520-1-.07(3) provides that if a qualifying broker dies, resigns, or is discharged, the firm has 60 days to secure a new qualifying broker or must cease brokerage activity.

question: A firm's qualifying broker is discharged on May 1. The firm continues normal brokerage activity without securing a replacement qualifying broker through August 15 of the same year (well over 60 days later). Under Ga. Comp. R. & Regs. 520-1-.07(3), what is the compliance status of the firm at that point?
choice_a: The firm remains fully compliant, since Georgia law imposes no outer time limit for replacing a discharged qualifying broker
choice_b: The firm is compliant as long as it secures a new qualifying broker at any point before its next 4-year CE renewal cycle
choice_c: The firm is out of compliance -- it should have secured a new qualifying broker within 60 days of the discharge (by around June 30) or ceased brokerage activity, and continuing to operate more than 60 days later without a qualifying broker violates the rule
choice_d: The firm is out of compliance, but only because it also failed to notify GREC of the address change within 30 days
explanation: Ga. Comp. R. & Regs. 520-1-.07(3) gives a firm only 60 days from a qualifying broker's death, resignation, or discharge to secure a replacement, or it must cease brokerage activity. Continuing to operate more than 60 days after the discharge without a new qualifying broker in place violates the rule.
